title: Allium ampeloprasum Propagation Organ (Japanese Garlic): Polyphenol Profiling and Antioxidant Assessment Under Different Drying and Extraction Conditions
content: The genus Allium comprises more than 1,100 species, among which Allium sativum stands out for its nutritional and medicinal relevance. However, Allium ampeloprasum, including its propagation organ known as Japanese garlic, remains relatively unexplored despite increasing cultivation in Mexico. Agro-industrial processing generates byproducts, particularly skin shells from garlic, representing up to 30% of production and providing valuable bioactive compounds, such as polyphenols. This study evaluated phenolic profiles Ultrahigh Pressure Liquid Chromatography (UPLC), total polyphenol content by Folin-Ciocalteu, and antioxidant capacity using DPPH inhibition in skin shells, peeled, and complete propagation organs subjected to freeze or oven drying. Natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES), based on choline/glucose at 60% and 68% hydration were compared with methanol. NADES enabled selective antioxidant and anti-inflammatory compounds extraction. The highest total polyphenol content was obtained in freeze-dried skin shells extracted with 60% hydrated NADES (384.81 ± 15.38 mg GAE/100 g). The greatest DPPH radical inhibition was observed in freeze-dried skin shells with 68% hydrated NADES (93.08 ± 0.58%), where polyphenols like: Catequin, Chlorogenic acid, Rutin, Quercetin + Luteolin, Kaempferol, Hesperidin, stand out. These values highlight the A. ampeloprasum potential as an alternative phenolic compounds source as the results exceed those previously reported on Allium sativum's variety. The NADES feasibility, contributing to the crop's comprehensive ap-plication in the food, nutraceutical, and pharmaceutical industries.
